title: Words opening with p or f gather on paragraph first lines
statement: In paragraph text, the share of certain words whose first glyph is p or f is at least three times greater on the first line of a paragraph than on its other lines, and exceeds what is left when the words of each page are shuffled.
source: Sharpens F-003 after the red team's R-003: that attack reproduced paragraph-initial p and f with a writer who only sees where a line starts. This fact compares whole first lines with the other lines, so a writer who treats every line alike gives a ratio near 1. Public practice split: 15.4 (Zandbergen-Landini), 15.4 (Takahashi), 3.4 (RF, 223 words selected); public training pages 20.5, thirds of them 13.8 to 27.8. Decomposition on the training pages: p or f opens 51% of paragraph-first words, 2.6% of the later words on first lines, 1.3% of the first words of other lines and 0.25% of their later words; so about a tenfold excess remains on first lines after their first word is set aside, though the registered statistic includes that first word and so overlaps F-003. A line-restarting glyph chain with no knowledge of paragraphs gives 1.0 to 1.1 on the practice split and does not reproduce it: a target for generators that needs a paragraph-aware writer, not evidence of language.
